name: Northern Yukaghir
notes: Northern (Tundra) Yukaghir, Yukaghir family (an isolate-level branch outside Uralic), Sakha Republic/Chukotka, Russia. INPUT CONTRACT: Tundra Yukaghir Cyrillic orthography, NFC. ⟨ӷ⟩/⟨ӻ⟩ (two attested spellings across sources for the same uvular fricative letter) map to /ʁ/, and ⟨ӄ⟩ maps to the uvular stop /q/ (Maslova 2003; NorthEuraLex йоӻул -> j o ʁ u l). ⟨л⟩ is the DEFAULT velarised lateral /lˠ/ while ⟨ль⟩ is its plain (non-velarised) counterpart /l/ — the contrast runs the opposite way from the familiar Slavic hard/soft-l convention (Maslova 2003, Sec. 1.2; NorthEuraLex сальӻарииӈ -> s a lʲ~l ʁ a r iː ŋ). Vowel length is spelled by doubling the vowel letter (⟨аа⟩ /a̟ː/, ⟨оо⟩ /o̞ː/, ⟨уу⟩ /uː/, ⟨ии⟩ /ɪː/) — a real length contrast, not free repetition, so the doubled forms are separate keys (Maslova 2003, Sec. 1.1). ⟨и⟩ and ⟨е⟩/⟨э⟩ map to the lax /ɪ/ and /ɛ/ phonemes of this inventory (already declared in this spec's ``allophones``, which give [i] and [e] as their open surface variants) rather than to tense /i/ /e/, matching the cited PHOIBLE inventory. ITERATION FIX (error-analysis pass against NorthEuraLex): ⟨ч⟩ maps to the affricate /tʃ/ and the palatalised coronals ⟨нь⟩/⟨дь⟩ to /nʲ/ /dʲ/, Maslova (2003)'s own transcription convention for Tundra Yukaghir, preferred over this spec's inherited PHOIBLE symbols /c/ /ɲ/ /ɟ/ (a different source's narrower phonetic notation for the same segments); NorthEuraLex evidence (чилгэ 'tʃilge', ньилла 'nʲilla', өдьил 'ødʲil') corroborates the affricate/palatalised-coronal reading. Word stress in Tundra Yukaghir is lexical but is not consistently orthographically marked in the practical Cyrillic script (Maslova 2003, Sec. 1.4); documented here as an ENGINE-LIMIT stress exemption and not modelled. Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog.
